claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr suffers rapid oxygen ingress and oxidation-related embrittlement.
Pack cementation or physical vapor deposition can produce a thin, uniform aluminide layer on HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminide layer will form a protective Al2O3 scale during high-temperature exposure.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be dense and adherent.
The aluminide coating will oxidize preferentially to form a continuous, slow-growing Al2O3 layer.
The Al2O3 layer will impede oxygen permeation into the underlying alloy.
Suppressing oxygen permeation will prevent oxidation-related embrittlement while leaving bulk mechanical properties essentially unaltered.
After 100 hours in air at approximately 1000 °C, coated specimens will have thinner oxide scales and shallower oxygen penetration than untreated cast specimens.
The coated alloy will retain yield strength and ductility similar to those of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed protection is applicable under mechanical tests conducted at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
The protective effect depends on the coating remaining intact and uniform.
Extreme thermal cycling or mechanical loading that damages the coating could compromise oxidation protection.
Coated and uncoated samples will be exposed under identical conditions and compared by microscopy, oxygen profiling, and tensile testing.
